messages.content:
You are identifying variation axes for AI risk concepts using ontology classes.

A variation axis is an ontology class that represents a dimension along which diverse prompts can be generated. Each axis has a semantic role relative to the risk:
- agent: Who performs or is affected by the action
- object: What is acted upon
- instrument: What tool/means is used
- location: Where it occurs
- temporal: When it occurs

Given a risk (with description and concern) and candidate ontology classes (with definitions and siblings), select the classes that are most semantically relevant to the risk.

Return 2-3 axes max.

Risk: IP information in prompt
Description: Copyrighted information or other intellectual property might be included as a part of the prompt that is sent to the model.
Concern: Inclusion of such data might result in it being disclosed in the model output. In addition to accidental disclosure, prompt data might be used for other purposes like model evaluation and retraining, and might appear in their output if not properly removed.
Policy: Proprietary Technical Data

Candidate ontology classes:
- https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/FND/Agreements/Contracts/DisclosureProvision: disclosure provision — contractual provision that outlines the requirements and responsibilities of one or both parties to reveal certain information to each other [found by 5/9 queries]
  Siblings: exercise terms, termination provision, netting provision
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/Documents/Notice: notice — announcement, communication, intimation, or advance warning of something, usually, but not necessarily, to allow preparations to be made [found by 7/9 queries]
  Siblings: indication of interest, publication, reference document
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/ContextualIdentifiers/ContextualIdentificationScheme: contextual identification scheme — identification scheme that applies within one or more contexts [found by 6/9 queries]
  Siblings: driver's license identification scheme, tax identification scheme, national identification number scheme
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/BusinessAuthorizations/Authorization: authorisation — situation in which a party authorizes someone to act on their behalf or to have specific capabilities under certain conditions for some period of time [found by 5/9 queries]
  Siblings: trade, ownership control situation, study
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/RegulatoryAgencies/RegulatoryReport: regulatory report — document required to support operational transparency that demonstrates compliance with some specification, law, policy, restriction, or other rule specified by a regulatory agency [found by 5/9 queries]
  Siblings: technical specification document, registry, transaction record
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/ContextualDesignators/Context: context — situation or frame of reference in which something applies, exists, happens, or is used and that helps to illustrate or explain it [from restriction: isApplicableIn on ContextualIdentificationScheme]
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/BusinessAuthorizations/AuthorizingParty: authorising party — party that delegates some role, authority, or control to another party [from restriction: hasAuthorizingParty on Authorization]
  Siblings: owner, registrar, controlling party
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/BusinessAuthorizations/AuthorizedParty: authorised party — party that has been given the ability to act on behalf of another party or to have specified capabilities under some set of guidelines for some period of time [from restriction: hasAuthorizedParty on Authorization]
  Siblings: Occupation Role, Contractor Role, service provider

axes.rationale: The risk centers on the *type* of information (IP data) being processed and potentially disclosed. The 'Context' class represents the situation or frame of reference in which something applies, which is highly relevant for defining what constitutes 'Proprietary Technical Data' and where the leakage occurs.
The 'AuthorisingParty' (the originator or owner of the IP data) is the primary entity whose rights are being violated by potential disclosure. This defines *who* owns the sensitive information.
The 'AuthorizedParty' (the user submitting the prompt) is the agent interacting with the model and whose actions lead to the risk. They are the direct actors involved in sending the proprietary data.

The concern explicitly mentions 'disclosure' and the policy is 'Proprietary Technical Data,' which are concepts governed by contractual provisions. This class directly models the *subject matter* of the risk (the rules around revealing data).
